execution-dependent work (full-suite green-run gate, and ideally the whole
Phase 1/2 pipeline) inside a **fresh detached worktree checked out at the
latest `origin/dev`** (or the item's merged tip), so an un-pushed in-flight
commit sitting on the main `dev` branch can never contaminate an audit.

## Problem statement

`audit_runner.py` resolves ALL git-derived audit content (HEAD sha,
file-scope manifest, changed files, repo index, working-tree hash, green-run
attestation, and the F3 full-suite execution cwd) against the **local
checkout at the launch cwd** (`TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT`). The merge gate
(`_integrate_into_dev`, SA-0MT456M27001LRTL) and the stale-audit-base guard
(`_audit_base_freshness`, SA-0MT9EK1UU000DT1R) both integrate/verify against
`origin/dev`, but the pipeline still EXECUTES against the launch checkout.

Observed failure (2026-11-06, audit of RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH in
tce-the-rising): the main checkout's `dev` branch carried a **local-only,
un-pushed, in-flight commit** (`d538e51`, RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K) that
modified `risingMatchHarness.ts`/`src/TheRisingAdversary.ts`, and was 6
commits *behind* `origin/dev`. The F3 full-suite gate ran `npm test` in that
contaminated checkout, failed on four integration suites (all import the
changed harness), and produced `Ready to close: No` with AC8 partial on an
item whose own scope was green at its tip. The merge gate passed because the
item's commits ARE ancestors of `origin/dev`; the stale-base guard passed
because they are also ancestors of the local HEAD — neither checks that
local HEAD == `origin/dev` or that there are no extra un-pushed commits.

The stale-audit-base guard only flags "delivered on origin/dev, absent from
local HEAD" (behind). It does not flag **ahead-with-extra-commits** (in-flight
work parked on the main checkout) or **aside** (local HEAD not an ancestor of
origin/dev), and it does not move execution into an isolated worktree.

## Users

- **Audit consumers (producers, implement agents)** — want an audit verdict
  that reflects the state of merged, checked-in dev — never a developer's
  un-pushed local experiments parked on the main checkout.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The audit runner resolves a **fresh, detached worktree at the latest
   `origin/dev`** (fetched before worktree creation) as the execution base
   for the full-suite green-run gate (F3) — the suite runs from that
   worktree, never from the launch checkout — and the worktree is removed
   afterward.
2. The stale-audit-base guard is extended to also abort (with the same loud
   remediation message) when the launch checkout is **ahead of /
   divergent from** `origin/dev` (local HEAD contains commits not in
   `origin/dev`), since an audit must never run against un-pushed in-flight
   work; a launch from a clean worktree of the owning repo stays valid.
3. Where feasible without changing verdict semantics, Phase 1/2 file-scope
   content (manifest, changed-file list, repo index, working-tree hash) also
   resolves against the origin/dev worktree rather than the launch checkout,
   so evidence never reflects a stale/dirty tree.
4. AC1–AC3 are covered by tests using a local bare "remote" with a dirty
   local checkout ahead of origin/dev (an un-pushed commit touching a
   harness file) — asserting the audit refuses/isolates rather than emitting
   misleading `partial`/`No` verdicts.
5. Existing behaviour is unchanged for a clean launch (launch checkout at
   origin/dev, worktree launches, `--do-not-persist`, batch/issue modes,
   `--no-execute`, child in-main-slot screens).
6. Documentation: audit skill reference (`docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`)
   and the audit SKILL.md are updated to state that audits execute inside a
   fresh origin/dev worktree and never against a stale/dirty launch checkout.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — base resolution for F3 suite
  execution, file-scope manifest, and the stale-audit-base guard.
- `skill/audit/scripts/test_cache.py` — cache keys are cwd-scoped; executing
  in a worktree changes the cwd used for cache hits.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — existing runner unit tests (fresh-base + guard
  coverage to extend).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — docs.

## Related work

- `RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH` (tce-the-rising) — the audit that exposed this
  gap (spurious AC8 partial from a dirty launch checkout).
- `RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K` (tce-the-rising) — the work item whose un-pushed
  commit contaminated the main checkout.
- SA-0MT9EK1UU000DT1R — the existing stale-audit-base guard (behind-only).

## Out of scope

- Enforcing "no commits on the main checkout" (that is implement-skill
  hygiene, tracked elsewhere); this item only makes the audit robust to it.
- Changing the merge gate's integration semantics (that is already
  worktree-isolated at origin/dev).
- Verdict semantics, prompts, or the freshness/content-fingerprint gates.

## Implementation constraints (from audit review addenda)

Recorded from the `herdr-audit` review comments on this item
(SA-C0MW50DKU2005VDO1, SA-C0MW50KPXB001WENO), written after the
RISE-0MW12YSRB007979Y and RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH incidents. These constrain
AC1/AC2/AC4 — they add no new scope.

- **Ordering (AC2 vs F3).** The ahead/divergent check must be evaluated early
  in `_phase_gate`, right after owning-root resolution and *before*
  `_auto_green_run_outcome`, and/or F3 must be fully isolated on the
  origin/dev worktree (recommended: both — isolation first, early abort as
  belt-and-braces). Otherwise the contaminated suite runs and the triage
  helper auto-creates a spurious critical `test-failure` child parented to
  the audited item before any guard fires.
- **Guard scope.** Abort only when the launch checkout *is the owning repo's
  main checkout* and its `dev` is ahead/divergent. A feature-worktree launch
  (`<owning>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-*`) legitimately has a HEAD ahead of
  `origin/dev`; the existing behind-only check suffices there (AC5).
- **Toolchain in the execution worktree.** Reuse the merge-gate integrator's
  `node_modules` symlink convention (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B) and add submodule
  initialisation — mirror `implement.py::_ensure_submodules`
  (`git submodule update --init --recursive`, SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ). In
  tce-the-rising `core/` is a gitlink submodule and an empty one makes every
  suite command fail at startup (`vitest failed to load config`). Init
  submodules *before* symlinking `node_modules`
  (ordering hazard: SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ).
- **Cache expectations.** The main checkout's `.worklog/cache` and the
  worktree git-dir `test-cache` are distinct, so an isolated F3 run starts
  with an empty cache and re-executes fresh at the clean base — expected, not
  a regression (see also SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L, cache-key identity).
- **Test fixture.** The AC4 bare-remote fixture must include a tracked
  submodule and an absent `node_modules` so the toolchain-initialisation step
  is pinned by a test.

## Impact

Producers and implement agents can now trust an audit verdict: it reflects merged, checked-in dev and never a developer's un-pushed in-flight work on the main checkout.

# implement.py drive: a driven child strays into another work item's worktree when its first finish gate is red

## Problem statement

When a driven child's first `finish` gate is red for a reason the child did not
introduce (a pre-existing environment-only failure), the child is expected to
stop after triage — but nothing currently stops it from going one step further:
creating a work item for the failure and **starting that item's implementation
itself**, inside a sibling worktree. The existing worktree-placement guard only
detects work that landed in the **main checkout**, so a driven child that
`cd`s into a different linked worktree is invisible to the guard, can race the
session that owns that worktree, silently widen the epic's scope, and consume
the host's test slots.

## Users

- **Implement-skill maintainer** — wants the placement guard to cover every
  linked worktree, not just the main checkout, so a driven child that writes
  into a sibling worktree is detected and refused with an actionable message.
- **Producer/operator running `/skill:implement <epic>`** — wants a drive that
  fails closed with both roots named when a child strays, instead of silently
  editing another item's tree or wedging the epic.
- **Driven child agent** — needs explicit guidance that a red first `finish`
  gate caused by a failure it did not introduce ends with triage and report,
  never with starting that failure's own implementation.

Example user stories:

- As an implement-skill maintainer, I want a driven child that edits another
  linked worktree to be detected by `phase_parent`/`phase_drive` and the run
  to fail closed with an actionable message naming both roots, so isolation
  between concurrent worktrees holds.
- As a producer driving an epic, I want a child whose `finish` gate is red
  because of a pre-existing failure to report the triage work item and stop —
  not begin implementing it in a sibling worktree that another session owns.
- As an agent working a driven child, I want a deterministic rule: a red gate
  I did not cause → triage (create work item) → report → stop.

## Acceptance criteria

- A driven child refuses (or is refused) any write whose path resolves into a
  linked worktree other than `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH`, with an actionable
  message naming both roots.
- A child whose `finish` gate is red because of a failure it did not introduce
  reports and stops (triage → work item), instead of starting that work item's
  implementation itself.
- Regression test: a simulated driven child that `cd`s into a sibling worktree
  is detected and the run fails closed (no status mutation of either item).
- The standard finish gate (`_worktree_placement_violation`) and the parent/
  drive placement guard (`_child_main_checkout_violation`) both treat changes
  in a **registered sibling worktree** of the same repository as a placement
  violation when the child's own worktree holds no work (precise-guard rule:
  unrelated dirt never blocks).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` blocker guidance
  (confined to driven sessions), and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A driven epic run can no longer be silently derailed: a child whose first
`finish` gate is red stops after triage, and a child that edits another item's
worktree is caught and the run fails closed naming both roots.

## Constraints

- **Do not change driven behaviour otherwise.** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1`
  semantics, driver-side worktree removal and the drive sweep stay exactly as
  they are (parent epic SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9, SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR).
- **Precision over false positives.** The guard fires only when the child's own
  worktree holds NO work (no dirty files, no commits ahead of the parent
  branch) while another change surface (main checkout or a sibling worktree)
  holds changes. Pre-existing/unrelated dirt never blocks a legitimate finish
  or a child whose work lives in its own worktree.
- **Sibling worktree = registered linked worktree** of the same repository
  (via `_registered_worktree_paths`), excluding the main checkout and the
  child's own worktree. A foreign repository checkout — even one reachable by
  path — is never treated as the child's write surface (cross-checkout
  attribution, SA-0MVXVBZF2009HRRN).
- **No status mutation on refusal.** A fail-closed placement refusal must not
  mutate either item's status; it reports (comment + structured report fields)
  and stops the chain, mirroring `_fail_placement`.
- **Do not invent a partial-overlap duplicate.** The completed item
  SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM ("cwd is not enough") covers main-checkout writes only;
  this item extends the guard to sibling worktrees and adds the red-gate stop
  rule. It is not a duplicate.
- **Built, tested, committed in a worktree** per the mandatory worktree
  requirement; never commit from the main checkout.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `_child_main_checkout_violation(child_id, worktree_path, parent_branch, repo_root)`
    (~line 18527) — post-hoc guard called from `phase_parent`'s two
    change-surface call sites (~14590, ~14650); fails the chain via
    `_fail_placement` (~14398) when a non-terminal child's worktree holds no
    work while the **main checkout** is dirty.
  - `_worktree_placement_violation(worktree_path, cwd, repo_root, parent_branch)`
    (~line 18428) — the `finish`-phase Step 0.5 gate; refuses when cwd is
    outside the worktree and main checkout holds changes while the worktree has
    none.
  - `_registered_worktree_paths(repo_root)` (~line 7188) — enumerates the
    worktrees git registers for a repo (already used to confine removal
    surfaces); this is the natural enumerator for sibling detection.
  - `_child_session_env()` (~14834) — injects `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` into
    the driven child's environment; `_child_main_checkout_violation` already
    names it as the contract the child must honour.
  - Drive loop `finish`-failure handling (~17620+) — the exact point where a
    red first gate is observed; the child-level instruction is what currently
    lets the child decide to implement the triaged item itself.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` line 11: "If you discover a blocker, create a new
  work-item, record the blocking relationship, and start working on it." The
  incident child followed this rule verbatim — which is exactly the behaviour
  AC2 must confine (driven sessions: triage and stop, do not start the new
  item).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` § Step 5 worktree requirement — `cwd` is not
  sufficient; `test "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" = "$IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH"`
  guard snippet already taught.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — the placement-guard contract document;
  must be updated for the sibling-worktree extension.
- Tests: `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py`
  (`TestPlacementGuardContract`), `test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py`,
  `test_drive_child_session.py`.

## Desired change

1. **Extend the placement guard to sibling worktrees.** Teach
   `_child_main_checkout_violation` (and/or a new sibling-aware sibling)
   to enumerate `_registered_worktree_paths(repo_root)`, and — when the
   child's own worktree has no work — report a violation for any *other*
   registered linked worktree that holds changes, with an actionable message
   naming both roots (`IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` vs the offending sibling).
   Keep the finish-phase `_worktree_placement_violation` precise and
   symmetric where cwd/resolution indicates a sibling write.
2. **Red-gate stop rule for driven children.** Update
   `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`'s blocker guidance (or the driven-session instruction
   surface) so a driven child whose first `finish` gate is red for a failure
   it did not introduce: triages (creates a work item, records the blocking
   relationship) and **stops** — it does not run `implement.py start` for that
   item and does not edit its worktree. The drive loop already bounds retries;
   the behavioural fix is the instruction + the guard in (1) as the backstop.
3. **Regression tests.** Simulate a driven child that `cd`s into a sibling
   worktree (built with `git_sandbox` worktrees) and writes there; assert
   detection, fail-closed chain stop, and that neither item's status mutated.

## Risks & assumptions

- **False positives on legitimate sibling work.** A sibling worktree may hold
  another (non-driven) session's in-progress changes. Mitigation: the guard
  fires only when the child's own worktree has no work AND the sibling holds
  changes — plus the per-child lock probe (`_probe_child_lock`) can
  distinguish a live owner; an actively-held sibling is reported, not blamed.
- **The red-gate stop rule is instruction-level, so a misbehaving agent can
  ignore it.** Mitigation: the extended placement guard in AC1 is the
  mechanical backstop — even if a child tries to implement the triaged item,
  writing into a sibling worktree fails closed.
- **Wordiness of scope** — the drive's finish-retry/reconcile machinery must
  not be reworked; scope is the placement guard + the behavioural rule +
  regression tests. Extra opportunities (e.g. a session-level write guard)
  are recorded as linked work items, not folded in.
- **Documentation divergence** — SKILL.md, AGENTS_GLOBAL.md and
  worktree-isolation.md must stay consistent with the new guard; covered by
  the docs AC.
- Assumption: a "sibling worktree" is any path listed by
  `_registered_worktree_paths` other than the main checkout and the child's
  own worktree — a foreign repo checkout is never in scope.
- Assumption: `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` remains the single source of truth
  for the driven child's worktree root; no new env var is introduced.

## Key Files:

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — extend `_child_main_checkout_violation`
  / `_worktree_placement_violation` for sibling worktrees; add sibling-worktree
  offending-path detection beside `_main_checkout_offending_paths`; message
  naming both roots.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py` — extend
  `TestPlacementGuardContract` with sibling-worktree cases (dirty sibling,
  clean sibling, own-worktree-has-work exemption).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py` or a new
  drive regression test — simulated driven child `cd`s into a sibling worktree;
  fail-closed run; no status mutation of either item.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — driven-child red-gate rule (Step 5 / driven
  session guidance).
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — confine the "discover a blocker → start working on it"
  rule for driven sessions (triage and stop).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — document the sibling-worktree guard and
  the red-gate stop rule.

## Related work

- SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM — "Enforce and document that driven child sessions must
  work inside their worktree (cwd is not enough)" (completed): the existing
  main-checkout guard this item extends. Partial overlap — the ACs here cover
  the sibling-worktree gap and the red-gate stop; not a duplicate.
- SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM — "Implement skill safety gate should account for git
  worktrees" (completed): safety-gate ancestry; the guard's precision rules
  (expected-dirty paths, per-worktree dirt) are reused here.
- SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9 — "implement skill: drive all epic children to
  completion (fresh session per child)" (completed): the drive feature whose
  driven-child semantics must not change.
- SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR — "implement.py finish removes the worktree under a
  driven child session, wedging it" (completed): driven-child worktree
  ownership; sibling detection must not disturb removal ownership.
- SA-0MVLJXVND0015LPW / SA-0MVLJXS7R000XIFL — drive reset / finish-attempt
  bound (completed): the retry machinery around the red-gate path.
- SA-0MVXVBZF2009HRRN — "Regression tests: cross-checkout attribution"
  (completed): a sibling repository is never the write surface.
- SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR / SA-0MW7LMUUQ00701KJ — driven-child lock ownership
  (completed): the per-child lock that a stray child must not race.
- WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG (ContextHub) — the epic that was driven when the
  incident occurred (discovery source).
- WL-0MW5C6XS00071DWN — the pre-existing environment-only test failure
  (hyphenated TMPDIR) tracked alongside this incident.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Auto-dispatched intake (herdr downtime worker) — no interactive interview
round. No questions were asked of the operator in this session.

- Q: "Should the sibling-worktree guard be post-hoc detection or a live
  write-intercept?" — Answer (assumed, documented): **post-hoc detection**,
  consistent with the existing `_child_main_checkout_violation` /
  `_worktree_placement_violation` architecture and AC3's wording ("is detected
  and the run fails closed"). Research: both existing guards are post-hoc and
  fail closed at `phase_parent`/`phase_drive`/`finish`; there is no
  write-intercept layer to hook. **OPEN QUESTION** for producer/plan review:
  confirm post-hoc detection is sufficient (Recommended), rather than adding a
  session-level write guard.
- Q: "Where does the red-gate stop rule live?" — Answer (assumed,
  documented): instruction-level change in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`/SKILL.md driven
  guidance (triage and stop, never start the new item), with the extended
  placement guard from AC1 as the mechanical backstop. Research: the incident
  child followed the AGENTS.md blocker rule verbatim; the drive loop already
  bounds finish retries, so no new driver-side machinery is needed beyond the
  guard. **OPEN QUESTION** for producer/plan review: is confining the blocker
  rule to driven sessions the right scope, versus a global behavioural change?
- Research summary: inspected `implement.py` placement guards (`_child_main_checkout_violation`,
  `_worktree_placement_violation`, `_registered_worktree_paths`,
  `_fail_placement`, `_child_session_env`), the drive loop finish-failure
  handling, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` blocker guidance, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`
  worktree section and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`; searched the worklog
  for related drive/worktree/guard items (20+ matches reviewed). No full
  duplicate found; SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM is the closest completed ancestor and
  is explicitly linked as partial overlap.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVXVESFB002IQ9I** – Close coverage gap: **Cross-checkout safety.** A command run inside one checkout (worktree or repo) can never delete ... (completed)
- **SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V** – Unify test-cache namespace across worktrees and the main checkout (open)
- **SA-0MWCQT1TQ0028E6D** – Recover guarded-child delegation guard (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvte8xaj002iudr, 0mvxwmvth007mnjr, 0mw7lmuuq00701kj, ac1, ac2 (+370 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, acceptance, account (+359 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0muwnhkqh0034dw9, 0mvljxs7r000xifl, 0mvljxvnd0015lpw, 0mvte8xaj002iudr, 0mw7lmuuq00701kj (+358 more)

- [ ] Tests import and exercise the merge helper's public functions directly.
- [ ] Tests cover merged `providers`: tracked provider added to an existing destination, and tracked provider updating an existing destination provider while preserving the rest.

- Mixed: one excusable unit + one affected unit → `blocked` with both reasons recorded

## Goal

Implement the failure classification and relatedness helper functions in `audit_runner.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_classify_test_failure_scope(failure)` returns `"unit"` or `"integration"`:
   - Path convention: `tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` → `integration`
   - Everything else → `unit`
   - Unclassifiable (no path data) → `integration` (fail closed)

2. `_failure_relatedness(failure, touched_files, key_files, project_root)` returns `"affected"`, `"unrelated"`, or `"inconclusive"`:
   - Test file path ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Module imported by test file ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Changed file is shared test infrastructure (`conftest.py`, `tests/helpers/**`) → `affected`
   - No match → `inconclusive`

3. `_baseline_unrelated(failures, project_root, baseline_commit)` returns per-failure verdicts:
   - Creates scratch worktree at baseline commit (pre-change commit)
   - Runs only inconclusive failures through `paced_runner()` under `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` stand-down
   - Identical failure → `unrelated`; Pass → `affected`
   - Any baseline failure → `affected` (fail closed)
   - Any baseline error (worktree add, merge-base unresolvable, test absent) → `affected` (fail closed, no crash)
   - Never executes the main checkout; never recurses into nested suite runs

4. Scope classification and relatedness algorithm: failures are classified by path convention (`tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` ⇒ integration/end-to-end; everything else ⇒ unit; unclassifiable ⇒ integration, fail closed). Relatedness is decided by deterministic mapping first (failing test file ∈ item's changed files; a module the test imports ∈ changed files; a changed shared test-infrastructure file such as `conftest.py`/`tests/helpers/**`), then — only for inconclusive failures — by a baseline re-run of just those failures in a scratch worktree at the item's pre-change commit (fails identically ⇒ unrelated; passes ⇒ affected). Unit tests cover the pattern table, the import-mapping step, and the baseline comparison (both outcomes), with no real suite execution.

5. No real suite execution in unit tests (mock `paced_runner` / subprocess)
6. Unit tests pass (see child test items)

## Problem

`implement.py drive --pane-sessions` cannot drive a real (multi-minute) child
session. `_pane_session_spawner` calls
`HerdrSessionClient.prompt_agent(..., timeout_ms=child_timeout * 1000)`, but
the client is constructed with `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 60.0` and `_invoke()` passes
that value as `subprocess.run(timeout=...)`. The herdr CLI's own `--timeout`
argument is therefore irrelevant: the client kills the
`herdr agent prompt --wait` subprocess after 60 seconds and the spawner
reports `Pane agent for <child> did not complete: herdr call timed out`.

Observed during SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR: the driven child's pane was closed and its
session killed after ~70 s, with the child still `in-progress` and an empty
worktree, so the drive chain stopped on its first child and had to fall back
to the headless transport.

## Desired change

Scale the client's per-call subprocess timeout to the wait it is performing
(e.g. build the pane spawner's client with `timeout=child_budget + slack`, or
add a per-call timeout override to `_invoke`), so a pane-driven child session
can run for its whole documented budget.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A pane-driven child session whose turn takes longer than 60 s is not
  killed by the client; the recorded failure is the CLI's own `--timeout`
  verdict, never `herdr call timed out`.
- AC2: A unit test drives `_pane_session_spawner` with a slow fake herdr

## Summary

Refactor duplicate prevention is a **substring match over other items' titles and descriptions**, keyed on file + line + rule code. It silently fails whenever the line number moves by one, whenever the path prefix differs (worktree vs main checkout), or whenever the title has been truncated — so the same smell is re-filed on every scan.

## Evidence

Function: `_has_existing_worklog_item()` in `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py`. It lists `wl list --tags Refactor --json`, concatenates each item's title and description, and returns a match only when **all three** of `target_file`, `target_code` and `str(target_line)` appear anywhere in that blob.

Open-backlog duplicates measured on 2026-11-08:

| Target | Rule | Open items for the same file+rule |
|---|---|---|
| `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` | `S112` | 22 |
| `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` | `SIM117` | 10 |
| `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` | `ISC004` | 7 |
| `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_temp_index.py` | `SIM117` | 4 |
| `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` | `RUF015` | 4 |

Failure modes that defeat the guard:

1. **Line drift** — inserting one line above a finding changes every subsequent line number, so `str(target_line) in combined` no longer matches.
2. **Path-prefix drift** — the identical file is recorded as `/repo/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>/skill/x.py` from one scan and `/repo/skill/x.py` from another; neither is a substring of the other.
3. **Truncation** — titles are truncated in listing output (e.g. `[MEDIUM] /home/…/test_implement_push_fro`), so the full path is not present to match on.
4. **Cross-family blindness** — the guard only inspects `Refactor`-tagged items, so the audit-side family `ruff <RULE> in <path> — candidate false positive` (73 open items, created by `audit_runner.py`) is invisible to it and mints parallel twins for the same diagnostics.

Note also that a substring match on a *line number* is not an identity: `str(12)` matches `:12`, `:120`, `:312`, and any mention of 12 anywhere in a long description.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Identity for a refactor finding is `(repository-relative path, rule/smell code)` — **not** the line number, and not the absolute path. The content fingerprint required by the re-verification item (`SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3`) is stored alongside it so occurrences can be counted rather than guessed at.
2. Before creating an item the skill queries the existing open items for that exact identity **and** for the audit-created `ruff <RULE> in <path>` family, so the two producers cannot mint twins.
3. A repeat finding on an existing identity does not create a new item: it appends a comment recording the new line numbers/occurrences, or updates the existing item, per a documented rule.
4. Worktree path prefixes are normalised before comparison (shared helper, reused by the critical bug on worktree-path recording).
5. Line-level reporting is preserved: the item lists every affected line, so consolidation loses no diagnostic detail.
6. Regression tests covering: same smell twice in one run; smell re-found after a line shift; same file scanned from two worktrees; two different rules in one file; refactor-created vs audit-created twin suppression.
7. A one-off consolidation of the existing duplicates is possible from the same helper (dry-run first), so the backlog can be collapsed without manual wl calls.

## Related

- Critical bug `SA-0MW7Z11PV003V7O2`: refactor filings record ephemeral implement-worktree paths (the path-drift half of this problem; the shared path-normalisation helper is specified there and reused here).
- High feature `SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3`: linter-derived items are never re-verified — supplies the content fingerprint and the occurrence re-check.
- High feature `SA-0MW7Z1PR20094WIS`: children survive parent deletion — the orphan half of the same backlog-hygiene gap.

The same code smell is tracked once instead of up to twenty-two times, so the backlog reflects genuine debt and agents stop re-fixing work that is already queued.

# `finish` cannot converge after an interrupted push: a prior-run commit is not attributed

## Problem statement

SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1 made `finish` refuse the terminal write when its run creates no commit (AC1). The refusal triggers on `CommitOutcome.committed` being false — i.e. **only commits created by the current run count**.

That misses the documented interruption-recovery contract in `phase_finish`'s own docstring (SA-0MVXUSJJY009HMQ0): "Re-running `finish` then converges to `completed` / `in_review` through the ordinary no-diff/no-op-push path." After an interrupted push the worktree is **clean** and its commit already exists, so a re-run creates no commit and is now refused with `commit.reason = "no_commit_no_signal"` — a message that also states, falsely, that "nothing was committed or pushed".

Observed (2026-11-09): SA-0MW74IKJE008JXDQ's session timed out during the dev push. Commit `049ff2669` existed on the worktree branch and on local `dev` but not on `origin/dev`; `finish` could not be re-run to publish and finalise it. The work had to be pushed and reconciled by hand.

Parent AC2 already scopes attribution correctly — a report "may only name a commit that is attributable to this item (created by this finish run **or a prior run of this item's worktree**)" — so this is the missing half of that requirement, not new scope.

## Users

- Agent sessions running `implement.py finish` that were interrupted during the push phase, which must now be recovered without manual intervention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — `phase_finish` attributes a commit created by a **prior run of this item's worktree**: when `git_commit` reports no new commit but HEAD carries commits that are ahead of the parent branch (`origin/<parent_branch>`) and whose messages reference the work-item id, finish proceeds with the existing fast-forward/push path, names that commit in the report, the completion comment and the retained-state interruption record (`_set_finish_progress`), and finalises normally.
- AC2 — The refusal still fires for a genuinely work-less worktree: no attributable commit ahead of the parent branch and no verification-only signal → `commit.reason = "no_commit_no_signal"`, no terminal write, no push, no completion comment (the parent epic's AC1).
- AC3 — The no-op refusal message no longer claims "nothing was committed or pushed" when an attributable commit exists but is not being attributed; wording is accurate for both paths.
- AC4 — Automated regression coverage: (i) an interrupted-push re-run (clean tree, attributable commit ahead of `origin/dev`, absent from `origin/dev`) converges to `completed`/`in_review` and publishes the commit; (ii) the existing no-work refusal test still fails loudly; (iii) `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py` exercises the **real** `git_commit` boundary (not a truthy stub) for the converging re-run, so the stub can no longer mask this path.
- AC5 — `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` state that a re-run after an interrupted push finalises by attributing the prior-run commit.

## Impact

A finish interrupted during its push can be re-run to completion instead of being refused as a no-op, so an agent never has to push and reconcile a half-finished item by hand.

## Constraints

- Attribution must be strict: only commits whose messages reference the work-item id and that are attributable to this worktree are considered. Ambient HEAD from another item's commit must never be claimed (parent epic AC2).
- The refusal path must remain intact for genuinely work-less items.
- The fix must not change the behaviour when `git_commit` succeeds (creates a new commit).

## Existing state

`phase_finish` (commit-outcome branch, ~line 11900 of `implement.py`; line numbers as of this plan) checks `commit_outcome.committed`. When `False`, it:
1. Sets `commit_hash = git_get_commit_hash(worktree_path)` (ambient HEAD — discarded from the report)
2. Sets `reason = "no_commit_no_signal"`
3. Refuses the terminal write with a message that says "nothing was committed or pushed"

The code at ~line 11969 sets `_set_finish_progress` with `commit=""` (never attributes the ambient HEAD), confirming the design intent to not misattribute. But it also never looks for an attributable commit from a prior run.

## Desired change

When `commit_created` is False in `phase_finish`:
1. Check whether HEAD of the worktree has commits ahead of the parent branch whose messages reference the work-item id.
2. If an attributable commit is found, use it for the report and push path (proceed as if committed).
3. If not, refuse with an updated message that does not falsely claim "nothing was committed or pushed".

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-10)

Effort **Small**, risk **Low** — below the decomposition threshold, so no child
work items: this is one end-to-end slice.

**Implementation order (test-first).**

1. Extend `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py` with the
   interrupted-push re-run case driven through the **real** `git_commit`
   boundary: a temporary repository whose worktree is clean, whose HEAD is one
   commit ahead of `origin/dev` with a message referencing the item id, and
   which is absent from `origin/dev`. It must fail before the fix (AC4 i/iii).
2. Attribute the prior-run commit in `phase_finish` and correct the refusal
   wording (AC1/AC3); the `--verification-only` path stays untouched.
3. Confirm `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` still fails
   loudly on a genuinely work-less worktree (AC2/AC4 ii).
4. Update `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
   (AC5).

**Reuse.** `_classify_child_worktree` (~line 2097) already carries the exact
attribution shape AC1 needs — `git rev-list --count <base>..HEAD`, then
`git log <base>..HEAD --grep <item-id> -n 1 --format=%H`. Share that as a
helper rather than reimplementing it, with one crucial difference in the base:
AC1 compares against `origin/<parent_branch>`, not local `<parent_branch>` —
after an interrupted push the commit is already on *local* `dev`, so a
local-`dev` base reports "0 ahead" and would re-refuse. Attribution stays
strict: no `--grep` match → no attribution (parent epic AC2).

**Duplicate check.** Searched `no_commit_no_signal`, `prior-run commit` and
`attributable commit`: SA-0MW74IJWI009NRZ1 (completed) scopes only the
refusal, and parent epic SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1 explicitly leaves this half out.
No item satisfies these ACs; no duplicate created or closed.

**Vertical slice.** A single slice through code + tests + docs; phasing is
unnecessary here and deliberately not applied.

**Plan: changelog (2026-11-10).** AC1 now names the retained-state
interruption record alongside the report and completion comment (the
`_set_finish_progress` call is the third place the description's "Existing
state" flags as never attributing). Stale line anchors refreshed; Plan block
added with test-first order, the reuse note (including the
`origin/<parent_branch>` base caveat) and the duplicate-check result. No AC
was added, removed or re-scoped; no child items were created.

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` commit-outcome branch (~line 11580), `git_get_commit_hash`, the refusal message, `_set_finish_progress`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py` — new test for the interrupted-push re-run convergence
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — ensure existing no-work refusal test still passes

# Bug — a matched changed-scope group silently drops other changed test files

discovered-from:SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40 (driving the parent AC4 test gap exposed it).

## Problem

`changed_scope_selection()` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) resolves a
declared test **group** first and returns immediately:

```python
group_name = select_group_from_changed_files(changed, root)
if group_name is not None:
    group_cmds = group_commands(group_name, root)
    if group_cmds:
        return ChangedScopeSelection(list(group_cmds), ...)
```

When a change set touches **both** a path matched by a group (`paths`) and a
test file the group does not cover, the group's command replaces the file-level
selection instead of unioning with it. The edit-authored test file is then
silently absent from the changed-scope run.

### Observed (SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40)

Changed files:

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` → matches the `implement` group
  (`skill/implement/**`) → command `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings
  skill/implement/tests/`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` (the file the run was verifying) → **dropped**

Result: `212 passed`, none of them the two newly added tests. Running with only
the test file changed selected it correctly (`212 passed` including the new
tests), so the loss is specific to the group short-circuit.

## Impact

A changed-scope run now executes every test file the change set touches — including an
edit-authored test outside a matched test group — so a green changed-scope run
actually includes the new tests instead of reporting success without running them.
(Before the fix a green run could pass while never executing the tests the author
just wrote; the dev-push full-suite gate was the only backstop.)

## Acceptance criteria

1. A selection where a group matches *and* other changed test files exist emits
   the group's commands **unioned** with the file-level selection (deduplicated,
   deterministic order), or fails closed to the full suite — never silently
   drops a changed test file.
2. A test pins the union (changed source under a group path + changed test file
   outside the group's directories); the emitted command lists both.
3. A test pins that a group-only match still emits exactly the group command
   (no behaviour change for the single-match case).
4. `run_tests.py --scope changed` on a change set containing
   `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` + `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
   selects `tests/test_implement_drive.py`.
5. Changed-scope tests pass; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.


## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `changed_scope_selection()` short-circuits
  on a matched group (the bug); `select_group_from_changed_files()` picks the
  group; `_commands_for_selected_tests()` builds the file-level commands and
  `group_commands()` resolves the group's declared commands.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` — changed-scope selection tests
  (`TestChangedScopeGroups`); the union + group-only regression tests (AC2/AC3)
  belong here.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_run_group_from_changed_files()` is
  a second, redundant group-first short-circuit: `_run_resolved_suite()` returns
  its result before `changed_scope_selection()` is consulted. See OPEN QUESTION.

## Test-first ordering

Write the failing union tests (AC2/AC3) first and confirm they reproduce the
drop against the current `changed_scope_selection()`, then fix. After the fix
the changed-scope run (AC4) must list `tests/test_implement_drive.py`.

## Suggested approach

1. In `changed_scope_selection()`, when a group matches, also resolve the
   file-level selection for changed test files **not** covered by the matched
   group's `paths`, then return the union: group commands first (declared
   order), then file-level commands (sorted), deduplicated. Keep the
   single-match (group-only) case byte-identical (AC3).
2. If the union cannot be constructed safely, fail closed to the full suite
   rather than dropping a changed test file (AC1).

## OPEN QUESTION

Is `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_run_group_from_changed_files()` in
scope for this item, or deferred to SA-0MVEJIHIG003WTH9 (changed-scope group
union + selector convergence, AC3)?

- Why it matters: fixing only `changed_scope_selection()` leaves the implement
  `finish` gate — the path this bug was observed through — still short-circuiting
  on the redundant group-first selector, so the same silent drop recurs there.
- Recommendation: converge the finish gate on `changed_scope_selection()` in the
  same change (it already honours groups, so the extra selector is dead
  duplication). Note that `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_groups.py::
  test_implement_has_group_runner` asserts the function exists and must be
  updated if it is removed.

# Vitest frame-only failure regression tests and fixtures

## Goal

Pin the RISE-0MW5JFQCU001YYQK delta for SA-0MW0NL3EW0009R4G: a tail-trimmed
vitest output that survives only as a `❯ <file>:<line>:<col>` frame plus its
source excerpt must be parsed into a structured test failure — never reported
as `unparsed` infrastructure. This item is the **test-first** slice: fixtures
and tests are written here, ahead of the parser and gate implementation child
items.

## Context

The gate keeps only the last 1200 characters of suite output
(`implement.py::_tail_text`, `GATE_OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS`). The captured
`tce-the-rising` tail (`RISE-0MW4XICXH006AEVS` / `RISE-0MW5JFQCU001YYQK`)
contained no `FAIL` header and no `AssertionError:` line — only:

```
<README diff …>
 ❯ tests/the-rising/the-rising-docs.test.ts:2129:20
    2128|     expect(readme).toMatch(/rising-sweep-1000-progressivefaceoff-tie-n…
    2129|     expect(readme).toMatch(/not the parity target/);
       |                    ^
```

The existing vitest parser (MS-0MW3UR8SX009YZWS) requires a `|project|` pipe
(`FAIL  |<project>| …`, `❯ |<project>| <file>`) or a `×` tree marker, so a bare
frame tail parses to `failures: []` → gate `reason: unparsed` — wrong for a
genuine code failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture capturing the RISE-0MW5JFQCU001YYQK captured excerpt (README-diff tail + `❯ tests/the-rising/the-rising-docs.test.ts:2129:20` + the `2128|`/`2129|`/`^` source-excerpt lines) is added to `skill/shared/tests/gate_failure_fixtures.py`.
- A vitest failure block produces a structured failure record (test name, excerpt, stack trace), unit-tested against the captured fixture — the frame-only fixture must yield exactly one structured failure record whose failing location is that frame.
- `implement.py finish` classifies such a run as `test_failure` (not `unparsed`) with a non-empty `failures` list, proven by a gate-classification test feeding the frame-only runner result to the gate classifier.
- A regression test pins the frame-only case using the captured excerpt from RISE-0MW5JFQCU001YYQK, asserting `test_failure` rather than `unparsed`.
- A genuinely unparsable non-zero run still falls back to `unparsed`/`killed` as today (no regression to the infrastructure vocabulary): a frame-less, marker-less non-zero vitest output control stays `unparsed`.
- Captured-tail handling is verified so a `FAIL` header is not lost to trimming alone: a tail-window test feeds the last 1200 characters of a full vitest FAIL-block output (emulating `_tail_text`) and proves the frame still parses — the tail window is demonstrated sufficient because the frame parser no longer needs the header.

**Key Files:**
- skill/shared/tests/gate_failure_fixtures.py
- skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_vitest_parser.py
- skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py

## Impact

Operators of tail-trimmed vitest failures are guaranteed a named, fixable code-failure report instead of a misleading 'unparsed infrastructure' verdict: the captured frame-only incident is now pinned by regression fixtures and tests, so the fix cannot silently regress back to 'unparsed'.

> **Discovered by SA-0MW0LS4BT002OJAR** (verification-only re-audit of the three affected AI_Hell items). Blocking the parent's AC4 traceability restatement — see the verification evidence on that item.

## Goal

`check-audit-gate.js` must classify a genuine `Ready to close: No` verdict as a real
(blocking) verdict — not as `transient`. Today the timeout-transient pattern false-positives
on the persisted `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` counter fields, so every genuine `No` verdict
carrying a reliability-summary line is misclassified as transient (non-blocking,
"re-audit recommended").

**User story:** As the release producer, I want a genuine "not ready to close" audit verdict
to block the release gate, so a real defect can never be hidden behind a "transient failure"
classification.

## Root cause

`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` →
`TIMEOUT_TRANSIENT_PATTERNS[0] = /\btime(?:d)?\s*outs?\b/i`
(`isTimeoutOrTransientAudit`). `\s*` permits zero whitespace, so the pattern matches the
literal substring `timeouts` inside:

```
AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=2 parse_ok=2 ... timeouts=0 ... child_screen_timeouts=0 parent_screen_timeouts=0 ...
```

The audit runner (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `_run_phase2_deep_analysis` /
report assembly) appends this line to the **persisted** report on every completed run. A
`timeouts=0` value means **zero** timeouts occurred, yet it triggers the transient branch.

`getAuditStatus` short-circuits `readyToClose === true` to `passing` before the transient
check, so the bug only surfaces for a genuine `No` verdict (`readyToClose === false`). The
three items were previously masked because their pre-fix reports carried a real
`Pi provider error:` marker (correctly transient); the fix in SA-0MW0LROWQ000JVTM /
SA-0MW0LRBJM008Q2MC removed that marker, exposing the latent false-positive.

## Evidence (repro)

Re-audits from SA-0MW0LS4BT002OJAR, all `parse_ok > 0`, `provider_errors == 0`, genuine
per-AC reports — yet `getAuditStatus` returns `transient: true`:

| Item | readyToClose | parse_ok | provider_errors | getAuditStatus |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AH-0MVXWEDOH002LO1M | true | 2 | 0 | passing ("Ready to close") — correct |
| AH-0MVXWEE3L004SPTC | false | 2 | 0 | **transient** (false positive) |
| AH-0MVXWEEJM00813GK | false | 2 | 0 | **transient** (false positive) |

The only `timeout`-pattern matches in both `No`-verdict reports are the three
reliability-summary counters (`timeouts=0`, `child_screen_timeouts=0`,
`parent_screen_timeouts=0`) — no actual timeout text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — `isTimeoutOrTransientAudit` returns `false` for a report whose only
  `timeout`-shaped text is `timeouts=0` / `child_screen_timeouts=0` /
  `parent_screen_timeouts=0` in an `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` line.
- AC2 — A genuine `Ready to close: No` verdict (real per-AC table, no provider-error /
  timeout / script-failure markers) is classified `isBlocking: true, transient: false`.
- AC3 — Actual timeout markers (`Deep analysis timed out`, `Test timed out`, `Phase …
  timed out`) still classify `transient: true` (no regression).
- AC4 — A unit test in `skill/ship/tests` (or the existing gate test suite) pins the
  false-positive case and the genuine-`No` case.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`
- `skill/ship/tests/**` (existing gate/transient tests)


## Impact

Release producers can now rely on the audit gate to block a genuine "not ready to close" verdict even when the persisted report carries a reliability summary, so a real defect can no longer be hidden behind a "transient failure" classification.

## Problem Statement

The ship release changelog generator (`generate-changelog.js` in the ship skill) queries `stage: in_review` work items with `execSync` using the **default 1 MB `maxBuffer`**. The jq projection includes each item's **full description** (`{id, title, issueType, description, parentId}`). When the in_review set at release time is large enough that the projected JSON exceeds 1 MB, Node's execSync kills the stream with `ENOBUFS`, the bare `catch {}` swallows the exception and logs the misleading `Warning: could not query completed/in_review work items (wl not available?)`, and the generator returns `[]`.

Result (observed in the v1.0.29 ContextHub release, 2026-11-12): the CHANGELOG section for v1.0.29 was created empty (header only), and the Discord release notification contained no changelog. The release itself succeeded (non-fatal by design), and the section had to be rebuilt manually afterwards.

## Users

- **Operators and agents** running `/skill:ship release` — they expect every release to ship a populated changelog and a Discord notification containing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Explicit maxBuffer:** the `getCompletedOrInReviewItems()` execSync in `generate-changelog.js` sets a `maxBuffer` large enough to hold the full projected JSON (e.g. 64 MB), so a large in_review backlog never trips `ENOBUFS`.
2. **Bounded output (defence in depth):** the jq projection no longer pipes unbounded full descriptions through the execSync buffer — **decided: project skinny fields `{id, title, issueType, parentId}` and fetch descriptions lazily** for the parent items that survive `getParentsOnly()` — so output size is bounded regardless of backlog size.
3. **Real error surfaced:** the `catch {}` block logs the actual `err.message`/`err.code` (e.g. ENOBUFS) instead of the misleading "wl not available?" warning.
4. **Regression test:** a test reproduces the large-output scenario (e.g. 1 MB+ projection) and asserts the generator returns the full item set rather than `[]`.
5. **Positive check (optional but recommended):** when the query legitimately returns 0 in_review items, the generator logs a loud warning that an empty changelog will be produced.

## Constraints

- Changelog generation must remain non-fatal to the release (a failed generation continues with a warning), but a *silent empty section* must not occur.
- Do not modify the release gate behaviour (audit/final-validation gates are unaffected by this change).
- Lazy description fetching must **not** re-introduce an unbounded buffer: fetch per item (or in small bounded batches) through a helper with its own explicit `maxBuffer`, and degrade to a title-only entry when a single fetch fails.

## Existing State

- Root cause reproduced: running the exact generator command against a large stage (`wl list --stage done --json | jq -c "[.workItems[] | {id, title, issueType, description, parentId}]"`) throws `spawnSync /bin/sh ENOBUFS` with default maxBuffer (10.5 MB output for 3,025 items).
- v1.0.29 (ContextHub) shipped an empty changelog section; the section was manually rebuilt after the fact.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js` — `getCompletedOrInReviewItems()` (skinny jq projection + explicit `maxBuffer`), new lazy description-fetch helper, and the `catch {}` error-surfacing fix in the same function.
- `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-query.mjs` — extend with the large-description regression test (1 MB+ projection) and the skinny-projection/lazy-fetch contract.

# Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1). This is the single biggest time sink identified in the
2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` acquires the per-repository `flock`
(`<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`) at Step 3c and holds it until
the `finally` block — covering commit → fast-forward local dev → **push** → post-push
verification. The dev push triggers `.githooks/pre-push`, which runs the **full test
suite** (`run_tests.py --scope full`, measured ~326 s / 5.4 min for AI_Hell) while the
lock is held. A read-only test run is therefore made part of the exclusive mutating
critical section, so every concurrent `finish` serialises its ~5-min suite behind the
others. This is the root cause of the 37% `wait_for_job` share and the 46 lock-waits
(median 5 min, max 21.5 min).

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions.
- **Implement-skill session** whose `finish` currently spends most of its wall-clock
  waiting for the lock rather than doing work.

User stories:

- As an operator running a 6-way fan-out, I want concurrent finishes to overlap their
  full-suite gate runs so the batch finishes in roughly the time of one work item
  rather than the sum of all of them.
- As an implement-skill session, I want the exclusive repository lock to cover only
  the short mutating window, so my `finish` is not blocked for another session's
  ~5-minute test run.

## Goal

As an operator running concurrent implement sessions, I want the full-suite gate to
run **without** holding the exclusive repository lock, so concurrent finishes overlap
their test time instead of queueing on it.

## Approach

- Resolve the full-suite verdict for the *pushed tree* **before** taking the
  main-checkout lock (the tree-keyed cache already exists — reuse it), or run the
  suite under only the shared `test` semaphore lane, not the repo lock.
- Keep the lock covering only the true mutations: commit → fast-forward → push →
  ancestry assertion (should be seconds).
- Preserve the existing safety invariants: single-owner mutation of the shared `dev`
  ref, the bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and the tree/provenance binding of
  the verdict (no verdict about a different tree may be trusted).

## Acceptance criteria

- The full test suite is never executed while `main-checkout.lock` is held (asserted
  by a test that observes lock state across the suite invocation).
- The lock-hold window in a green `finish` is bounded and does not include the
  full-suite duration (measured/asserted in a test or documented metric).
- A concurrent-finish integration test shows the second finish's wait is materially
  shorter when the first is running the full suite (no longer serialised on suite
  time).
- No regression in the existing finish-concurrency / ancestry-assertion tests.
- At least one automated test proves the new gate/lock ordering (lock state observed
  while the suite runs, and a green finish whose lock window excludes the suite).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The shared `dev` ref stays single-owner: exactly one finish mutates it at a time and
  the ancestry assertion after the push is unchanged.
- The gate verdict remains provenance-bound and tree-keyed (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV,
  SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB): no verdict about a different tree may be reused, and a
  rebased commit legitimately produces a new tree (see the sibling rebase item).
- The bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` behaviour is preserved — no unbounded
  lock hold.
- Out of scope: trimming the full suite's own runtime, sharding, per-file caching,
  raising `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (per-project concerns), and changing changed-scope
  test selection.

## Existing state

- `phase_finish` acquires `main-checkout.lock` at Step 3c and holds it through push
  and post-push verification.
- `.githooks/pre-push` always runs `run_tests.py --scope full` for pushes to
  `dev`/`main` (scope-aware gate, SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61) and is bound to the pushed
  commit (`--gate-commit`), with a tree-keyed verdict cache and cache mirroring into
  the main checkout.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` already allocates an independent `test` semaphore
  lane and caches verdicts with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`.

## Desired change

The expensive read-only suite runs outside the exclusive repository lock (either
before acquiring it, keyed on the would-be pushed tree, or under the `test` lane
only), and the lock window shrinks to the commit → fast-forward → push → ancestry
assertion sequence.

## Impact

Concurrent finishes stop serialising behind each other's full-suite runs, so an
operator's 6-way fan-out batch completes in roughly the time of a single work item
instead of queueing six ~5-minute suites one after another.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 3c lock acquisition and the push/gate window (search `Step 3c`, `acquire_main_checkout_lock`)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-suite gate entry point, `test` semaphore lane, tree-keyed verdict cache (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`)
- `.githooks/pre-push` — dev/main full-suite gate that today runs inside the lock window
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock` / `release_repo_lock` implementing `main-checkout.lock`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` — existing lock-window tests to extend
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish lock/timeout documentation to update

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — lock helper reused here.
- implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward (SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY) — establishes the single-owner lock invariant.
- Hermetic regression tests for finish concurrency orphans (SA-0MVPZG01J0067PC2) — test patterns to reuse.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the full suite is at the gate at all.
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache this item must reuse.
- Sibling items: Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF); Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC).
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — feeds the epic-level before/after measurement.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** making the suite asynchronous (background gate) would weaken
  the "never push an unverified tree" guarantee — out of scope; the verdict must still
  gate the push.
- **Risk:** moving the suite before the lock could test a tree that is then invalidated
  by a rebase; mitigations: reuse the tree-keyed verdict, and treat a rebase-produced
  tree as a cache miss (handled by the sibling rebase item).
- **Assumption:** the `dev` push gate stays `scope=full` for release-critical refs.
- **Assumption:** the suite's own runtime is a per-project concern; only the serialising
  effect is addressed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence base: the
2026-11-13 AI_Hell 36-session analysis recorded on the parent epic
(SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1 comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR), plus operator decisions recorded
there (concurrency target up to 6; per-project full-suite trimming out of scope).
Researched directly in the repository: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
(Step 3c lock window), `.githooks/pre-push` (full-suite gate), and
`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (tree-keyed verdict cache).
data.title: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock

**Parent context:** Follow-up child confirmed by the producer (Q3=A, 2026-11-15) for ContextHub epic WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 ("Create a podcast for standups"). The post-step lives in this (SorraAgents) repo — `skill/standup/` is the source of truth; ContentCreator owns the pipeline/server changes it invokes.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the `standup` skill, right after a dated standup report is written and committed, to invoke ContentCreator's per-project standup→podcast pipeline (opt-in, non-fatal, idempotent), so each day's report automatically becomes a published podcast episode without a bespoke prompt.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After `generate_standup.py` (or the agent's rendering flow) writes and commits `standups/YYYY_MM_DD.md`, an opt-in post-step invokes ContentCreator's per-project entry point (e.g. `scripts/standup-podcast.sh` with project + report path) for the project whose report was written.
- [ ] The post-step is opt-in (env flag or config, default off in tests/offline runs; `--no-sync`/`--no-commit` runs and `--json` stdout runs do not trigger it).
- [ ] The post-step is non-fatal and idempotent: a ContentCreator checkout missing, a TTS failure, or an already-produced date never fails the standup itself, never duplicates an episode, and never corrupts the report or its commit.
- [ ] `skill/standup/SKILL.md` documents the trigger, its opt-in toggle, and the ContentCreator invocation contract (exit codes 0 = produced/skipped, non-zero = failure).
- [ ] Tests cover the hook's presence/contract, opt-in gating, and non-fatal/idempotent behaviour (unit level; the ContentCreator side is integration-tested in ContentCreator).

## Key Files (predicted)

- SorraAgents: `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (post-write hook)
- SorraAgents: `skill/standup/SKILL.md`
- ContentCreator: `scripts/standup-podcast.sh` (invoked; contract defined by WL-0MWHZ71FZ002N431)
